tier1_postgresql.purpose: real multi-connection transactional acceptance, owner authority, ambiguity, generation-bound and cross-window owner-current history reconciliation, physical PITR, authenticated-principal single-winner surviving-authority recovery evidence and Tier 1 relocation activation authority

tier2_timescale.purpose: candidate tenant isolation, background jobs, fresh-cluster restore, target-owned key generation/checkpoint/freeze authority, era-aware canonical relocation projection, bounded cross-authority activation verification and bounded capacity falsification

classification_basis.final_package_gate_requirement: The exact final package HEAD, including reviewer documentation, must independently rerun both gates before review or acceptance.
classification_basis.note: The executable anchor proves owner-controlled source/poll authority; owner-derived history finality/currentness whose coverage is bound to the exact current authority generation and invalidated on every generation transition even when timestamps remain equal; stable reconciliation identities validated before provider-time windowing so owner-current corrections cannot evade conflict checks by moving across a requested window boundary; surviving external authenticated PITR recovery grants consumed through an ID-only authority API whose grant facts are resolved internally and whose single-winner identity is derived from authenticated session authority rather than caller-supplied target/principal data; recovery principals have no direct grant-table read privilege; same-principal retry convergence and different-principal rejection under concurrent races and credential-spoof negatives; genuine fresh-cluster Timescale reconstruction; lock-before-F source fencing; deterministic self-delimiting structured cryptographic representations whose typed timestamp representation is injective across PostgreSQL AD/BC eras; target-owned checkpoint signing authority whose effective key is generated inside Tier 2 and is neither provisioned nor retained by the cross-database test controller; Tier 1 verification without mint capability; restricted authority-owned verifier connection capability state with verifier secrets absent from function source; caller-local post-connect verification deadlines with stalled peers failing closed; durable Tier 1 activation grants; target promotion only after exact grant verification; no uncheckpointed pre-activation target history; seal-vs-DML serialization; and atomic rollback of the Tier 1 placement+grant commit when a grant conflict is injected.

max(target)=F cannot prove complete target coverage
history completeness requires contiguous coverage from supported_history_floor

conflicting owner-current provider content under an existing reconciled observation identity must reject before recording coverage
target rows above F before activation must be rejected or included in checkpoint authority

late_history_evidence.worker: history_reconcile_worker NOLOGIN with EXECUTE only on sweep/finalize
late_history_evidence.sweep_authority: worker supplies only window plus expected authority generation; actual generation and provider snapshot are read and locked from provider_authority
late_history_evidence.finalization_authority: try_finalize accepts no caller authority/finality/currentness values; it reads and locks current authority_generation, finality and required snapshot from provider_authority
late_history_evidence.stale_worker: rejected when expected generation differs from durable current authority
late_history_evidence.coverage_generation: only reconciliation_run rows whose authority_generation equals the exact currently locked owner generation are eligible
late_history_evidence.generation_transition: every authority-generation advance clears materialized coverage and moves non-gap state to reconciliation_required even if snapshot/finality/currentness timestamps are unchanged
late_history_evidence.coverage_semantics: only overlapping/touching runs from the exact current authority generation whose durable provider_snapshot_at satisfies owner-required currentness form continuous coverage
late_history_evidence.stable_identity_content: existing accepted (stream_id,observation_id) content is immutable; owner-visible observed_at or numeric_value mismatch rejects the sweep before a reconciliation_run is recorded
late_history_evidence.cross_window_identity_validation: stable identity conflict validation precedes provider-time insertion filtering; a conflict is checked when either accepted observed_at or owner-current provider observed_at intersects the requested sweep window
late_history_evidence.cross_window_negative: accepted 11:58 identity corrected by owner-current provider to 12:01 is rejected by an 11:55..12:00 sweep; accepted content remains unchanged and no reconciliation_run is created
late_history_evidence.conflict_failure_atomicity: rejected conflicting sweep preserves accepted canonical content and does not mint coverage
late_history_evidence.same_timestamp_generation_negative: generation 3 reuses generation 2 timestamps but cannot reuse generation 2 coverage; a fresh generation 3 sweep is required before finalization
late_history_evidence.unrecoverable_retention_loss: explicit durable gap; never false complete

recovery_evidence.restore_boundary: physical PostgreSQL PITR to committed R
recovery_evidence.surviving_authority: separate external control PostgreSQL not included in source backup/restore
recovery_evidence.grant_storage: structured typed columns: domain, R, F, successor epoch, placement version, required receipt, nonce, canonical payload, attestation, claimed authenticated principal and claim timestamp
recovery_evidence.grant_canonical_field_encoding: UTF-8 byte length in decimal + ':' + lowercase UTF-8 hex
recovery_evidence.grant_canonicalization: all structured fields are independently self-delimiting before HMAC-SHA-256
recovery_evidence.grant_authentication: HMAC-SHA-256 with random key generated and stored only in surviving external authority
recovery_evidence.delimiter_collision_negative: legacy pipe framing admits ambiguous logical field boundaries; the self-delimiting encoding distinguishes them
recovery_evidence.tampered_external_grant: rejected and cannot claim the grant
recovery_evidence.claim_api: claim_grant(grant_id) and verify_claimed_grant(grant_id); no caller-supplied target/principal identity or signed grant facts
recovery_evidence.credential_spoof_negative: rival password cannot authenticate under winning recovery principal role name
recovery_evidence.grant_claim_semantics: surviving authority loads and verifies the grant internally under row lock; first authenticated session principal claims, same-principal retry returns true, different authenticated principal returns false
recovery_evidence.grant_claim_concurrency: dedicated concurrent race between two independently authenticated principals against one grant requires exactly one winner
recovery_evidence.successful_admission: requires reconciled local R state plus a fresh successful authenticated single-winner claim of the surviving externally held structured canonical grant by the same surviving-authority principal that later verifies the claim
recovery_evidence.evidence_identity_mechanism: PostgreSQL LOGIN/password sessions provisioned after restore reaches R

relocation_evidence.source_fence_derivation: placement authority locked before F is derived
relocation_evidence.source_inflight_acceptance_race: acceptance holding placement lock commits before fence and is included in F
relocation_evidence.canonical_field_encoding: UTF-8 byte length in decimal + ':' + lowercase UTF-8 hex
relocation_evidence.canonical_timestamp_encoding: UTC YYYY-MM-DDTHH24:MI:SS.USZ plus explicit AD/BC era before canonical_field framing
relocation_evidence.timestamp_era_negative: 0001-01-01 BC and 0001-01-01 AD canonical timestamps are distinct on both Tier 1 PostgreSQL and Tier 2 Timescale
relocation_evidence.canonical_timestamp_cross_store: PostgreSQL and Timescale canonical_timestamp produce identical values for the same BC or AD timestamp
relocation_evidence.digest_era_aware: authoritative_digest and target_digest both call canonical_timestamp before canonical_field
relocation_evidence.canonical_serialization: ordered rows; every field self-delimiting; row concatenation uses no delimiter as an authority boundary
relocation_evidence.cross_store_encoding: PostgreSQL and Timescale produce identical canonical_field output for text containing literal 0x1f/0x1e control bytes
relocation_evidence.canonical_payload_fingerprint: SHA-256 over deterministic self-delimiting canonical observation serialization
relocation_evidence.checkpoint_attestation_payload: domain, tenant, F, checkpoint id, generation, sealed flag, target count, target digest and target max are independently canonical_field encoded before HMAC
relocation_evidence.checkpoint_attestation_cross_store: Tier 1 canonicalizer and Timescale issuer produce identical canonical_checkpoint_payload for the same facts
relocation_evidence.projection_writer: ts_automation_owner with projection DML but without checkpoint/key ownership or freeze-disable authority
relocation_evidence.target_signing_key_generation: generated inside Tier 2 target authority using target-side randomness
relocation_evidence.target_verifier_capability: yes/no SECURITY DEFINER verification only; verifier cannot read signing key or target connection capability state
relocation_evidence.tier1_verifier_capability: yes/no SECURITY DEFINER activation-grant verification only; verifier cannot read grant/placement tables or Tier 1 connection capability state
relocation_evidence.target_connection_capability_store: restricted target-authority-owned state; target verifier cannot read
relocation_evidence.tier1_connection_capability_store: restricted Tier1-authority-owned state; projection writer and target verifier cannot read
relocation_evidence.checkpoint_attestation: domain-separated HMAC-SHA-256 over self-delimiting target-owned checkpoint facts
relocation_evidence.preseal_future_row: any target row accepted_ordinal > F makes sealing fail and leaves control phase open
relocation_evidence.sealed_phase: all target-history DML for the relocating tenant is rejected and target self-activation without a Tier 1 grant returns false
relocation_evidence.tier1_activation_commit: placement transition and exact activation grant are committed in one local PostgreSQL transaction; conflict raises and rolls both back
relocation_evidence.activation_conflict_fault_injection: duplicate grant conflict after placement UPDATE path proves fenced placement survives, injected grant cannot activate target and target remains sealed
relocation_evidence.target_activation_authority: target verifies exact committed Tier 1 grant and matching active placement before sealed-to-activated transition
relocation_evidence.cross_authority_call_order: remote verification occurs before local authority locks; after verification each authority performs short local transactional/CAS work only
relocation_evidence.cross_authority_failure_semantics: connection failure, established-call local deadline expiry, disconnect, verifier error or uncertainty returns false/fail-closed
relocation_evidence.established_call_deadline_evidence: five-second remote delay probes are issued through asynchronous dblink polling with a 500 ms local probe deadline; both directions return false well below 1.8 seconds
relocation_evidence.evidence_verifier_transport: PostgreSQL asynchronous dblink plus random LOGIN verifier credentials, connect_timeout=1 for connection setup, caller-local post-connect polling deadlines, and restricted authority-owned connection capability stores
relocation_evidence.activated_phase: existing history is immutable; INSERT is eligible only above the relocation fence
relocation_evidence.seal_dml_serialization: target DML takes target_control shared authority; seal takes exclusive authority before future-row check and digest

crypto_evidence_boundary.rule: every structured message protected by hash/HMAC must first have deterministic versioned injective or equivalently unambiguous field framing, and each typed value must itself have an injective canonical representation over the full accepted domain; cryptographic integrity is not a substitute for canonical structure
crypto_evidence_boundary.canonical_encoding: bounded evidence representation using UTF-8 byte-length plus lowercase hex for observation payload fields, recovery-grant fields and checkpoint-attestation fields
crypto_evidence_boundary.timestamp_rule: relocation timestamptz canonicalization uses UTC microseconds plus explicit AD/BC era before field framing
crypto_evidence_boundary.target_checkpoint_hmac_sha256: bounded evidence integrity mechanism over canonical_checkpoint_payload with effective key generated and retained inside target authority
crypto_evidence_boundary.recovery_grant_hmac_sha256: bounded evidence integrity mechanism over canonical_grant
crypto_evidence_boundary.issuer_verifier_separation: verification capability does not include signing/mint capability; Tier 1 has no target signing key; cross-authority controller does not provision or retain the target key
crypto_evidence_boundary.verifier_secret_isolation: evidence verifier secrets are restricted authority capability state and are absent from SQL function source
crypto_evidence_boundary.production_requirement: accepted implementation may use equivalent encoding, typed canonicalization, crypto, recovery identity, verifier transport and secret storage only if independently reviewed evidence preserves deterministic versioning, injective full-domain typed representation including timestamp-era distinction, unambiguous structured representation, target-originated target-only mint authority, verifier-without-mint capability, secret isolation from callable function source and unprivileged principals, single-winner authenticated-principal recovery admission whose authority is not caller-supplied, bounded connection and established-response verification outside local lock windows, exact activation-grant binding, atomic Tier 1 grant+placement commitment and key isolation

privileged_automation_boundary.production_requirement: database connection/authentication admission, pg_hba/socket/network exposure and role-membership policy must prevent tenant/application principals from authenticating as or assuming ts_automation_owner

bounded_capacity_observation.interpretation: Mechanism-level bounded fitness evidence only. Production SLOs, retention, cardinality, sizing, cost and topology remain OPEN-REL-020 C3.

decision_recommendation.tier1: accept PostgreSQL Tier 1 mechanism only with immutable canonical observation content, owner-controlled source/poll authority, durable live poll claims, owner-derived provider finality/currentness, contiguous generation-bound reconciliation, invalidation on authority-generation transition, stable-identity conflict validation before provider-time windowing including cross-window corrections, rejection of conflicting canonical reconciled content, structured self-delimiting authenticated surviving recovery grants after PITR with an ID-only claim API and atomic single-winner authenticated-principal admission, lock-before-F relocation fencing, target verification without mint authority, and atomic durable activation-grant plus placement commitment
decision_recommendation.tier2: accept TimescaleDB historical projection only under the mediated shared-history profile, privileged automation-owner admission boundary, genuine fresh-cluster role reconstruction, complete target checkpoint equivalence, era-aware full-domain injective timestamp serialization, target-originated target-only checkpoint signing authority, rejection of uncheckpointed target data before activation, target promotion only after exact Tier 1 activation-grant verification, immutable pre-F history after cutover, restricted verifier capability secrets, caller-local established-response deadlines, and cross-store self-delimiting checkpoint representations
rejected_assumptions: caller or worker supplied timestamps are not provider finality/currentness authority
same snapshot timestamp does not make reconciliation coverage valid across owner authority-generation changes
an existing reconciled observation identity with changed canonical content is not an idempotent duplicate
provider-time window filtering must not hide a stable identity conflict when the accepted and corrected timestamps straddle the requested sweep boundary
a locally recreated post-R receipt is not surviving (R,F] recovery authority
an authenticated surviving recovery grant is not reusable bearer authority for multiple restored instances
a caller-copyable recovery target ID or principal name is not authenticated recovery authority
recovery principals must not need direct grant-table reads or caller-supplied signed grant facts to consume authority
delimiter-parsed recovery payload text is not a structured cryptographic authority
max(target_ordinal)=F is not target completeness
target count/digest/max supplied by caller are not current target authority
identity-only digests are not canonical payload equivalence
delimiter-framed concatenation of unrestricted text is not an unambiguous canonical serialization
era-less timestamp formatting is not injective across the supported PostgreSQL BC/AD domain
a strong hash or HMAC does not repair ambiguous pre-crypto structured serialization
a Tier 1 verifier that holds the target HMAC key is not independent target verification
a key stored only in the target database is not target-originated authority if a cross-authority controller generated, provisioned or retained the effective key
verifier credentials embedded in SQL function source are not acceptable capability-secret isolation
connect_timeout does not bound a peer that connected successfully and then stopped returning a response
target automation cannot self-authorize sealed-to-activated without a committed Tier 1 activation grant
placement activation without an atomically committed exact activation grant is not valid successor authority
target rows above F may not exist invisibly before activation
PASSWORD NULL on a LOGIN role is not NOLOGIN or production connection-admission proof
same-cluster restore is not fresh role-topology recovery evidence
max(reconciliation window_to) is not contiguous history completeness
decision_recommendation.reversibility: Tier 2 remains behind the telemetry projection seam; replacement must preserve canonical observation identity/payload, deterministic versioned unambiguous structured serialization, injective typed canonicalization over the full accepted domain including timestamp eras, idempotent projection, owner-derived currentness, exact-generation reconciliation coverage, authority-transition invalidation, cross-window stable-identity content immutability, externally surviving recovery authority with single-winner authenticated-principal admission not derived from caller data, target-originated target-only mint/sign authority, verifier-without-mint capability, verifier-secret isolation, bounded established-response verification, target checkpoint/freeze semantics, exact durable activation-grant binding, atomic placement+grant commitment, privileged-infrastructure boundaries, tenant isolation and relocation/recovery semantics
